newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices ease despite tighter supply.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices ease despite tighter supply.

text.p: Thai rubber prices edged down this week amid thin demand and a softer tone in the Tokyo market and despite the current wintering season and tighter supplies, trade sources said on Friday.
There were active inquiries, both from China and Japan, but actual trading was modest, they told Reuters.
"Rubber moved in a narrow range all week with an upward bias, but the price was still lower compared to last week. The market was pretty dull," a Hat Yai trader said.
Although a firmer yen pressured prices, the market generally remained upbeat on confidence that real demand remained strong.
News that Japan's rubber imports from Thailand for January surged from December and went up 4.3 percent year-on-year boosted sentiment, they said.
Japan remained the biggest market for Thai natural rubber exports, accounting for about 34 percent of the country's total rubber exports.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for April shipment fell to 121-122 US cents a kg from 123 US cents last week. The concentrated latex price was steady at 93 cent a kg.
